convoLines.text: "Can I tell you something? At night I count the stars and name them after people."
There's an ease between you now — the kind that takes weeks to build.
"Thank you. I needed someone to know, and now someone does. Please keep it there. That's my read."
"Did you leave someone behind? ...Sorry. You don't have to answer that."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"Are you angry? At whoever did this. At the sky. At anything."
"I just — Good. Anger's fuel. Just — point it somewhere useful."
"Still on that question."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Alright. Catch you later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Did you sleep? I kept hearing things out past the treeline."
They go still. "So it's not just me. Good. That's... good to know. Bad, but good."
"I sleep in shifts now — two hours, up, listen, two more. My body learned it before my head agreed. Marseille, France never taught me that. The treeline did."
"Still on how you slept."
"Another time. The village needs me here."
"That can wait — it isn't going anywhere. What's on your mind?"
"Raul always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Okay, that's my quota of socializing."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You said you were furious. Most days. Still carrying it?"
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
"Here. I made an extra." Carolina presses something into your hand — a decent tool, oiled and kept. (Useful. Keep it.)
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on that personal stuff."
They let the words sit there, unanswered.
You show them Elderberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Raul is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Carolina grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Carolina is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"Sleep's gone strange. I tend the fire without being asked at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"Right. Go on, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Okay, real question: what's the funniest thing you've seen since we got here? I desperately need it."
They laugh — really laugh, the first real one you've heard in days. "Okay. Okay, that's good. I needed that."
"Me? I laughed yesterday and it scared me — the sound of it. Like my body remembered something my head hadn't approved. Laughter's a mutiny. A good one."
"Still on the funniest thing you've seen. …sorry."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Raul owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
You show them Elderberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"I save the best bite for last. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we got cut off, 7 days back. 'Sleep's gone strange. I tend the fire without being asked at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning.' We still owe that personal stuff a proper ending, too."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
Halfway to the ridge, Carolina freezes. Fresh tracks — big. "We go back now. Quietly." You do. The wild, reminding you.
"Next time I go out there, I tend the fire without being asked first. Calms the aim."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on what's been happening. ...sorry, I'm spiraling."
"What's the most useful thing you've learned since we got here?"
"The fundamental skill. Everything else is decoration."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Carolina is already 👁️ Scout — that promise is theirs.
"Alright, I'm listening. What's next?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You're family now. Chosen family — the kind that actually counts." "That's where we are."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"What got you through the first week? The very first days."
"Shock's underrated. It's the body's way of buying you time."
"Honestly? I don't think anything got me through. I just didn't stop. Some mornings that's the whole story — you keep not-stopping until not-stopping feels like a plan."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on what got you through the first week. …if that makes sense."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"...Never mind me. What were you going to say?"
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.
"I wasn't an ER nurse. I was a dry cleaner. It's safer if people don't know. Please don't tell the others."
Carolina nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Anyway — I should get going."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Same time tomorrow, maybe."
"You said shock got you through the first week. Just kept moving. What's carrying you now?"
"Take your time."
Their eyes do the math before their mouth does. You can see the calculation happening.
"I don't actually want to belong somewhere. I want to keep a record of everything. There are people from my old life I'd rather never find me. That's all."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."

"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that personal stuff. I mean it."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Have you felt it? Like the air before a storm, but — bigger. Something's on its way."
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
"I should go. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You said the most useful thing you learned is being hungry and going anyway. Still the lesson?"
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
It's quiet at the tree line. Carolina doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"As I said — we're still on that personal stuff."
Something in them stays shut, for now.
"Right — go on, I'm listening."
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They say the table's coming. For us. I keep thinking about what we'd even bring to it."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Ximena nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Sure. I'll be around."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

"Water's almost gone — 8 liters. I need someone to haul water with me at first light. Two of us, half the trips. Will you come?"

Sofia: "Hey — come here. You should hear this."
"Never mind the pantry run — we got it handled. Thanks anyway. We're down to 8 liters of clean water. Haul the creek with me at dawn? Two buckets each, there and back."
"Water's almost gone — 8 liters. I can't carry enough alone. First light, the creek, you and me?"
"I still need help with the creek water run."
Stand beside your partner first — same side of the Haven door — then help.
"Look, forget it. You wanted something?"
They glance toward the fire, toward the others — checking who's listening.
"I don't actually want to belong somewhere. I want to be remembered. I thought if you believed that, you'd trust me faster. I'm sorry. Or I'm supposed to be."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
They hear you out, but something in them stays guarded.
"Right. I get it." A beat — and then the subject is closed. They won't raise it again.
"Still on that water haul."
"Let me sit with all that. We'll pick it up later."
"Okay. I'll manage on my own."
"This was good." They mean it.

"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
"All right — let's ask them." You carry the proposal to The Red Table.

"Same. But keep your eyes open — some people here are performing, not surviving."
"Watch the quiet ones. Not the loud — the loud tell you everything. The quiet are either thinking or planning, and you can't tell which until it matters."

"Still on your read on people here."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."

Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.
"I'm not from Denver. I'm from Shanghai, China. I wanted an edge. You were new, you were listening, and I used it. I'm not proud of that."
"That again?" Sofia sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
"We went over this," Sofia says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Good — your read on people here, settled. Feels better said out loud."
"Same time tomorrow, maybe."
"So what's your plan here? Just... get through it?"
"Right, so — Honest. I can work with honest."
"Mine's simple: learn one useful thing a week. This week it's navigation. A plan's just a direction you argue with."
"Still on your plan here. That's the truth of it."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"That can wait — it isn't going anywhere. What's on your mind?"
"Good question." "Ximena always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."

Sofia nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Sleep's gone strange. I check everyone's shoes for wear at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Right. Action time. You know where to find me."

"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."

lines: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Raul Maldonado is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d41: 🕯️ Raul Maldonado is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: What Raul kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d41: "Raul's gone." Carolina looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Raul." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d41: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Arjun blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Wound Care (Level 1). Clean it, close it, cover it. Pressure stops bleeding. Clean water is better than dirty hands.
d41: ⚡ TECHNIQUE UNLOCKED: Precise Mend! Your healing knows where to go. +50% effectiveness. (Your knowledge of Wound Care amplifies your field_medicine.)
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Steady Hands (Level 1). Fine work under pressure. Dressing game, stitching wounds, tying snares — no shake.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Calming Panic (Level 1). Ground them: 5 things you see, 4 you hear, 3 you touch. Breathe with them. Slow is fast.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Managing Fear (Level 1). Fear is data, not orders. Acknowledge it, then decide anyway. Courage is fear that kept going.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Herbal Medicine (Level 1). Willow bark = aspirin. Yarrow stops bleeding. Plantain draws out infection. The pharmacy is outside.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Camp Cooking (Level 1). Cooking uses half the water, +10% kcal. Once per day: add a Secret Ingredient (a random inventory item) — 50% delicious (+morale), 50% educational.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Food Preservation (Level 1). Salt, smoke, dry. The big three. Salt draws water out; bacteria can't live without it.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: The Forager’s Eye (Level 1). You walk slower and see more. Food was always there; now you notice it.
d41: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Raul Maldonado, 41 days. The mantle passes to Arjun Shi.
d41: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Arjun Shi, 58 — an army medic. Their hands know different work now: Green Whisper, Beard Moss, Loud Chewer, Harvest Table, Berserker Rage.
d41: ◈ The System updates its file: the new bearer <redacted> "Feaster of the Living Garden." It had a word for this one before the Codex came.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Raul — and Raul is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d41: At the grave, Carolina, Sung, Ximena and 6 more speak for Arjun — "Raul trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d41: The fire knew Arjun before the Codex did — their name already carried weight here.
